# 0014 Make the decompiled engines fast to read

Status: todo

Owner's direction (2026-10-15): clean up the decompiled vendor code so that the owner, the orchestrator and subagents read and understand it faster: consolidate, remove, rename and tidy the files, structure them into subdirectories with their own README and CLAUDE notes where needed, for progressive disclosure. The decompiled output stays untracked (`CLAUDE.md`, "Sensitive data"), so everything here has to be regenerable from the scripts in `tools/ghidra/` plus tracked notes.

What there is now (2026-10-15): `work/re/decomp-x86_64/` holds 2710 files for the macOS engine, one per function, flat, named `Class__Method@address.c`: 382 `CAsic`, 284 `CRegistry`, 278 each for `CGL846`, `CGL128`, `CGL126`, `CGL125` (the register accessor classes, mostly one-liners), 156 `CScan`, 140 `CIOUSB`, 110 `CScanApi`, 48 `CAfe`, the AFE chip classes (`CWM8199`, `CES8140`, `CHT82V36`, `CAD9826`), `CMap`, `CAddOn`, `CRegister`, `CNotify`, and about 60 libc, CoreFoundation and thunk entries. `work/re-win/decomp-x64/` holds 2184 files for the Windows V5.0.2.0 engine, 1818 of them `FUN_<address>` without symbols, 112 `Unwind` stubs. Next to them: disassembly, function tables, call lists, string lists, scalar scans and the accessor facts, flat in `work/re/` and `work/re-win/`. The Ghidra output has known readability problems (`tools/ghidra/README.md`, "Notes on reading the output"): `this` shown as a named parameter when the method is not marked `__thiscall`, small constants printed as Mach-O header fields, and the virtual base casts `this + *(long *)(*(long *)this + -0x28)` (the `CRegistry` subobject) and `-0x20` (the `CIOUSB` subobject) on every line that touches the registry or the bus.

Deliverables:
- [ ] Layout, produced by the scripts: `work/re/macos/<Class>/<Method>@<address>.c` and `work/re/windows/<group>/...`, one directory per class or group, an `INDEX.tsv` per directory (address, name, file, one-line role where known), libc, CoreFoundation, thunk and `Unwind` entries dropped or moved to `other/`, the tables (function tables, call lists, strings, scalars, accessor facts, field tables) under `tables/` of each engine. The Windows `FUN_` functions grouped and named by the address map in `doc/vendor-driver/windows.md` where it exists, the rest left in `unnamed/`.
- [ ] Readability of each function: fix at the Ghidra level what can be fixed there (apply the demangled signatures so `this` is `this`, calling convention `__thiscall` on methods, the constant display problem) and post-process the rest with a script that rewrites the known idioms into readable forms (`registry(this)`, `usb(this)`, plist key names next to `CRegistry::<Key>` calls), so that a function like `CAsic::MotorSel` reads without decoding casts. The post-processor is a tracked Python script with tests on a few captured input snippets.
- [ ] Navigation notes, tracked in `doc/vendor-driver/engine/` and copied into the tree by the layout script: `README.md` at the root (which engines, which classes do what, how to find a function by name or address, what has been read so far with links to the documents that cite it), a `CLAUDE.md` for agents (start at the README, use the per-directory INDEX, never execute the binaries, cite function name and address), and one note per class that matters (`CIOUSB`, `CAsic`, `CScanApi`, `CScan`, `CRegistry`, `CGL126`, `CAfe`), listing the functions by role with the one-line verdicts already established in `doc/protocol/` and `doc/vendor-driver/`.
- [ ] `tools/ghidra/README.md` updated to the new commands and layout, and the existing documents' file name citations (`doc/protocol/playbook.md`, `serial-flash.md`, `serial-eeprom.md`, `macos.md`, `windows.md`) brought to the new paths.
- [ ] Review by a second agent: regenerate from scratch with the documented commands, confirm the tree and the notes match, and read three functions cold to judge the reading speed.

Related: `0005-vendor-driver-analysis.md`, `0012-driver-playbook.md` (the consumer of this layout), the owner's decision that the output stays out of git (`doc/log/2026-10-15.md`).
